MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE LA VERNE CITY COUNCIL
  Monday, December 4, 2023

At 6:00 pm, Mayor Hepburn kicked off the holiday season with a holiday message at the City’s
Christmas Tree Lighting Ceremony in front of City Hall along with Santa Claus and the Bonita High
School Chamber Singers.

A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by Mayor Hepburn at 6:33 pm.

Before the start of the meeting, Mayor Hepburn welcomed the audience to the Council Meeting in which
City business is conducted. He reminded everyone that per the City’s Rules for Decorum, all speakers,
members of the audience, and Council Members are to conduct themselves with decorum and to not
engage in conduct that interrupts the orderly conduct of the meeting. Also, he communicated that the
City of La Verne will not allow for public comment through Zoom until further notice. If you wish to provide
public comment for the meeting, please email your comments to citvclerk@citvoﬂaverne.org prior to the
start of the meeting. Public comments will be accepted at the meeting by those physically in
attendance at the appropriate time.

Council Members Present  Mayor Tim Hepburn
  Mayor Pro Tem Wendy Lau
  Council Member Rick Crosby
  Council Member Steven Frank Johnson
  Council Member Meshal “Kash” Kashifalghita

Absent:  None

Advisory Staff Present  Ken Domer, City Manager
  JR Ranells, Assistant City Manager
  Kimberly Hall Barlow, City Attorney
  Debra Fritz, Deputy City Clerk

Pledge of Allegiance was led by Steven Poe, U.S. NaVy E-4

Mayor Hepburn, on behalf of the City Council, presented to, Steven Poe, US. Navy E-4 a Pride of
La Verne Certiﬁcate of Recognition thanking him for his service to our country.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023,, Page» 2.

PRESENTATIONS

Legislative Updates for the  State Senator Susan Rubio provided a legislative update, highlighting
San Gabriel Valley  the more than $130 million dollars allocated to the San Gabriel Valley
  in various areas: Supporting Teachers, Workforce Development, and
  Building Community Parks, to name a few. She also helped fund a
  Regional Housing Trust which recently completed a housing project to
  support veterans and those experiencing homelessness.

Bonita High School Boy's  BONITA HIGH SCHOOL BOY’S WATER POLO 2023
Water Polo CIF Champions  The Bonita Boy’s Water Polo team ﬁnished with an overall record of
  24-12 for the season and placed second in the Palomares League.
  They advanced to the CIF playoffs where they had the number one
  seed and after 4 rounds of play, they advanced to the championship
  game where they won the Division 4 CIF Championship. They moved
  on to the CIF State Playoffs as the number one seed after 2 rounds
  and advanced to the finals where they defeated Pacific Palisades and
  won the school's ﬁrst Regional State Championship. The team was
  coached by Dillon Unsoeld and assisted by Gage Unsoeld, Joe
  Lampson, and Cody Lehotsky.

  Julian Falk  Braydon Jimenez  Max Distaso
  Jaxon Aggers  Jake Carlson  Matthew Humpert
  Gary Watson  Dylan Vegas  Jeffry Heaton
  Mavryck Mathis  Shane lbarra  Giancario Garcia
  Parker Montgomery  Jackson Dincin

  The team was honored with Pride of La Verne certiﬁcates and In N Out
  gift cards from the City Council, Senator Rubio’s ofﬁce also provided
  certiﬁcates of recognition for the Team’s Division 4 CIF win.

University of La Verne  UNIVERSITY OF LA VERNE WOMEN’S VOLLEYBALL 2023
Women’s Volleyball SCIAC  The University of La Verne volleyball team completed a historic season
Regional Runners—up  in 2023. The Leopards finished the season with a 25-5 overall record
  and a 13-3 record in the Southern California Intercollegiate Athletic
  Conference (SCIAC). The Leopards earned a spot in the NCAA
  Tournament and won their ﬁrst two games to advance to the Sweet 16
  where they ﬁnished as the regional runners-up. The Leos advanced
  further and won more games than any team since 2009. Four
  Leopards were named All-SCIAC (sky-ak) and three were named All-
  Region. Freshman Malia Capistrano was named the Region 10
  Freshman of the Year, sophomore Mya Ray was tabbed SCIAC
  Offensive Athlete of the Year and First Team All—American. The
  Leopards were led by the SCIAC Coaching Staff of the Year, head
  coach Jeff Hendershot, and assistant coaches Randi Taylor-Toomay.
  Mario Meza, and Jack Coberly.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023, Page 3.

  Nalani Young  Ayana Mier  Kiley McGarry
  Madison Smith  Isabella Walsh Zacky Coaston
  Sydne Humphrey  Kelly Yeung  Lauren Gott
  Kailin Katena  Lexi Giacobbe Kaitlyn Bloomer
  Noelani Soma  CC Flaherty  Malia Capistrano
  Julia Thomas  Mya Ray  Isabella Quiroz

  The team was honored with Pride of La Verne certiﬁcates and In N Out
  gift cards from the City Council, Senator Rubio’s ofﬁce also provided
  certiﬁcates of recognition for the Team.

At 7:06 pm, the City Council recessed and reconvened at 7:13 pm.

ANNOUNCEMENTS AND  Sherry Best, President of the La Verne Historical Society, announced
UPCOMING COMMUNITY  the December 16 Annual Vintage and Baked Good Sale, as well as the
EVENTS  Home Tour Event. Two historic homes will be open for tours.

  Yvonne Gallegos, Cultural Awareness and Social Inclusion Committee
  (CASI) member, announced the change of their meeting days to the
  ﬁrst Tuesday of every month at 5:00 pm. in the Citrus Room at
  Hillcrest.

  Danita Beauchamp thanked the community of La Verne for their
  support of the Wreaths Across America campaign. Continued support
  is needed to place the wreaths on the headstones, this will take place
  on December 16 after a small service with VFW members.

  Mayor Hepburn thanked Cynthia Gabaldon for her efforts to get
  commitments for the remaining number of wreaths they were short, to
  ensure the veterans were honored.

  Council Member Johnson announced the Church of the Brethren
  Christmas Concert, Sunday, December 10 at 4:00 pm. all are
  welcome.

  Council Member Crosby announced the Bonita Chamber singers will
  be performing their Yuletide Concert at the Methodist Church,
  December 5 at 7:00 pm. and Saturday, December 12 at 2:00 & 7:00
  pm. at Bonita Center for the Arts (BCA) Yuletide. The ULV Chamber
  Singers perform on December 10 at 4:00 pm. at the Morgan
  Auditorium.

  Council Member Meshal “Kash” Kashifalghita announced the Spark of
  Love is still accepting donations. Donation boxes are located at the
  Public Safety buildings, and City Hall. Crazy Bear Cycle will be
  donating bikes again this year. Bikes will be passed out at Hillcrest
  again this year.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023, Page 4.

  Council Member Crosby reminded everyone that VWnte-r Wonderland
  will be this Saturday, December 9 from 9:00 am. till 1:00 pm. at
  Heritage Park.

  Mayor Pro Tem Lau announced the Blood Drive at ULV, tomorrow
  December 5 from 10:00 am. to 4:00 p.m., also Tri-City Mental Health
  has a slew of events this month at their wellness center, please take
  advantage of this resource, they will be having a movie night this
  Saturday, airing The Grinch Who Stole Christmas.

  Mayor Hepburn encouraged everyone to take advantage of the
  information that is published regarding upcoming events, they can be
  found on our website and at the back of the agenda page. He thanked
  all the staff in various departments, Police, Fire, Public Works, and
  Community Services for the decorations on the buildings, he knows
  the staff and community appreciates see the lights and decorations.

  City Manager Domer announced the La Verne Link mobile application
  is available for download at the Google or Apple store, it’s an easy way
  to connect with the City and report such things as grafﬁti or potholes or
  other issues. The phone app is a direct connection to the City with
  access to community calendars and events.

  Mayor Hepburn announced the board meeting for the Public Financing
  Authority-EIFD is Wednesday, December 13 at 9:00 am.

CONSENT CALENDAR  It was moved by Crosby, seconded by Kash, and unanimously carried
  to accept, approve or act on the Consent Calendar items.

City Council Minutes  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES of the study session and regular City
  Council meetings of November 20, 2023.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City Council approve the minutes.
  Approved

Register of Audited Demands  REGISTER OF AUDITED DEMANDS for the following:

  In the amount of $1,819,873.23 dated November 8, 2023, and in the
  amount of $1,405,998.15 dated November 15, 2023.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City CounciIl approve the Register of
  Audited Demands. Approved

Resolution Cancelling the  RESOLUTION CANCELLING THE JANUARY 2, 2024, CITY
January 2, 2024, City Council  COUNCIL MEETING - The ﬁrst City Council Meeting in January 2024
Meeting  is requested to be cancelled due to lack of business after the holiday
  season. This item requires a resolution to cancel the meeting.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023, Page 5.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City Council approve the attached
  Resolution titled, “A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL, CITY OF
  LA VERNE, COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, STATE OF CALIFORNIA,
  CANCELLING THE JANUARY 2, 2024, CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING.” Approved

Authorize City Manager to  AUTHORIZE CITY MANAGER TO ADMINISTRATIVELY AWARD
Administratively Award  CONSTRUCTION CONTRACT FOR CDBG FUNDED CURB RAMP
Construction Contract for  ACCESSIBILITY PROJECT - This action will authorize the City
CDBG Funded Curb Ramp  Manager to execute a contract award for the Community Development
Accessibility Project  Block Grant (CDBG) funded Curb Ramp Accessibility Project to ensure
  completion of the project by the December 31, 2023, expenditure
  deadline. The total project costs are anticipated to be $288,000.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City Council authorize the City
  Manager to administratively award the CDBG-funded Curb Ramp
  Accessibility Project (up to $288,000) and execute any necessary
  documents, including amendments and change orders, subject to City
  Attorney review as appropriate. Approved

OTHER MATTERS

Legislative Platform for the  LEGISLATIVE PLATFORM FOR THE 2024 LEGISLATIVE
2024 Legislative Session  SESSION - Adoption of the 2024 Legislative Platform will help deﬁne
  the City's interests on priority issues and provide a framework for
  advocacy efforts at the federal, state, and local levels. The policy
  guidelines and statements included in the proposed 2024 Legislative
  Platform will allow City staff to address legislative and regulatory
  issues in a timely and focused manner.

  Mayor Hepburn called for Public Comment on this item.

  Danita Beauchamp asked Council to hold off on approving this item
  due to the dangerous verbiage in the legislative package.

  Joe Gabaldon opposes this legislative platform.

  City Manager Domer clariﬁed that items listed in the legislative wrap-
  up document are summaries of legislation signed by the Governor in
  2023, therefore they do not represent the proposed platform. The
  City's platform is very ﬁscally conservative, ﬂexible, and politically
  neutral. Anything the Council wants to debate would be brought forth
  at an open meeting for discussion to include public input. As part of the
  process, we always check with the Mayor before signing any letters of
  support. The platform gives us better parameters to make decisions on
  behalf of the Council.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4. 2023, Page 6.

  No further comments were received.

  Mayor Hepburn commented on how the COG also reviews the
  legislative bills and brings information to the City’s attention.
  information will be shared and discussed with the community.

  Council Member Crosby wants the public to have access to review the
  document, and wants to table item to next meeting, so residents will
  have more time to read the platform.

  Mayor Pro Tern Lau suggested an FAQ document be prepared and
  placed on the website to answer some of the questions of concern.

  Council Member Johnson felt more time was needed for our residents
  to review the document due to the timing of the Holiday season and
  wanted to postpone the item until January.

  Council discussed when to bring the item back. It was decided to bring
  the item back on December 18 for more discussion and then again on
  January 16, 2024, for possible ﬁnal action.

  Council Member Meshal “Kash” Kashifalghita agreed with giving more
  time to review for residents to get a better understanding.

  Council continued to discuss.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City Council approve the Legislative
  Platform for the 2024 legislative session. COUNCIL ACTION: Motion
  was made to continue this item to the December 18 meeting, so
  moved by Johnson and seconded by Lau, and unanimously carried.

REGIONAL  REGIONAL COMMUNICATIONS CENTER UPDATE - As has been
COMMUNICATIONS  summarized in the past, the Covina and La Verne Police Departments
CENTER UPDATE  are exploring options to consolidate their respective dispatch centers in
  an effort to regionalize police communication services and gain
  efﬁciencies in delivering this critical public safety service. This item
  provides an update on those efforts.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  Danita Beauchamp agrees with this change, dispatch jobs .are very
  difﬁcult.

  Council Comments.

  Mayor Hepburn supports this change.

  Council Member Crosby supports this item.

  Council Member Meshal “Kash” Kashifalghita also supports this item.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023, Page 7.

  Council Member Johnson, thanked Acting Chief Gonzalez and
  supports this idea 100%.

  Mayor Pro Tem Lau agrees this change is necessary.

  RECOMMENDATION: That the City Council receive and ﬁle this
  Agenda Report. Council action: Moved by Crosby and seconded
  by Kash and approved unanimously (5/0) to receive and ﬁle.

PUBLIC COMMENT  This is the time set aside for anyone wishing to address the City
  Council on items within the jurisdiction of the City Council which are
  not listed in any other place on the agenda. Under the provisions of the
  Brown Act, the legislative body is prohibited from talking or engaging in
  discussion on any item not appearing on the posted agenda. However,
  your concerns may be referred to staff or placed for discussion at a
  later date. Please email your public comment to the City Clerk’s Ofﬁce
  at citvclerk@citvoﬁaverne.org; Your public comment will be shared
  with the City Council and included as part of the permanent record.
  There is a 3-minute time limit on public comments.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment.

  Jay Bernard commented on the trains blowing their whistles from San
  Dimas Canyon to White Street, too noisy.

  Rich Gill reminded everyone that this was the ﬁnal week to submit
  nominations for City Council for Districts #2 & #5.

  Barbara Smythe as part of the Diversity Committee wants City to be
  aware of labeling things Christmas, to be more sensitive to those in our
  community, try harder to use Holiday.

  Joe Gabaldon supports the legislative platform and thanked staff for
  the hard work. He also asked about the parking lot lights at vacant
  store locations not being on, and cars for sale parked along White and
  Wheeler Avenue. He commented on the possibility of using monies at
  the next election for an at large mayor to do a ﬁyer, similar to the
  holiday ﬂyer recently received.

  Yvonne Gallegos thanked the Council that came out and supported the
  Cultural Festival last weekend and followed up on the letter by the San
  Dimas Mayor against hate, and La Verne doing the same.
 City Council Minutes of the Regular Meeting of December 4, 2023, Page 8.

COUNCIL COMMENTS  Each Council Member may address the Council and public on matters
  of general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council
  Members to report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended
  per Assembly Bill 1234.

  Mayor Pro Tern Lau mentioned YFAC and encouraged the residents to
  participate. She enjoys the holiday decorations throughout the City
  and at City facilities, she mentioned the Cultural Festival event was a
  good experience, and hoped to see more attendees next year. She
  wished Council Member Crosby a “Happy Birthday” Council then sang
  happy birthday to him.

  Council Member Crosby commented on the YFAC meeting and the
  presentation that Tri City gave. The Police Department is looking for
  explorers, check out the PD website for more info. And the numerous
  Holiday singing events.

  Council Member Meshal “Kash” Kashifalghita mentioned this Saturday
  is the Fire Explorers ﬁrst day, and the upcoming Mosquito Vector
  Control Committee meeting he will be attending. Let him know of any
  concerns you might have. Senator Holden is hosting a toy and shoe
  drive to support other communities.

  Council Member Johnson is enjoying the new mobile app and asked
  that information on the upcoming election be included. The app has
  info on the E-Waste event Saturday, December 16, and you are able
  to report grafﬁti and other concerns.

  Council Member Crosby asked about the ﬁnal day of nominations,
  Friday, December 8. City Hall will be open for those who want to
  submit papers.

  City Manager Domer clariﬁed that staff will be on hand for anyone
  wishing to pull papers.

  Mayor Hepburn commented on the SGVCOG board meeting this
  month, including the Legislative caucus, SGV Regional Housing Trust
  that Senator Rubio donated to, the insurance commissioner info
  posted on website, a webinar is available, Cal Trans regarding
  highway conditions. He attended the wedding of our K-9 ofﬁcer
  Weinreb, a good time was had by all, Happy Holidays, spend your
  money in La Verne. The next Public Financing Authority meeting is
  scheduled for Wednesday, December 13 at 9:00 am.

Adjournment at 8:24 pm.

Respectfully submitted,
  Debra Fritz  é ‘
  Deputy City Clerk
